description: Three-component, epoxy-cementitious primer for damp substrates
whereToUse: Triblock P is used as a waterproofing treatment for damp substrates
old ceramic or terrazzo floor dressings on substrates with excessive residual humidity
highly-compact cementitious substrates with a residual humidity content higher than the level recommended for laying wooden, resilient and resin floors
treating damp concrete surfaces before applying protective and anti-corrosion epoxy products, or polyurethane dressing systems which are impermeable to water vapour
dressing concrete channels, drains and pipe-work
by adding 0.25 Quartz o 0.5 Quartz sand at a ratio of 1 : 0.5 for smoothing over uneven surfaces
notFor: Do not apply Triblock P directly on: · surfaces with free-standing water; · dusty, flaky, irregular surfaces with bleeding; · anhydrite or gypsum-based substrates; · old, cementitious or gypsum-based smoothing layers.
Do not apply Triblock P on cracks which are subject to movement, as the product is rigid and may also crack.
Do not use the product if the surrounding temperature or the temperature of the substrate is lower than +5°C.

technicalData.label: Mixing ratio
technicalData.value: comp. A : comp. B : comp. C = 12 : 38 : 50

technicalData.label: Waiting time between first and second coat
Waiting time before further applications
technicalData.value: from a minimum of 24 hours up to a maximum of 7 days

consumption.quote: 250-300 g/m² per coat on non-absorbent surfaces.
400-500 g/m² per coat on absorbent surfaces.

consumption.basis: per mm of thickness for smoothing applications
consumption.quote: 1.5 kg/m² per mm of thickness for smoothing applications.

mixing: The mixing ratio between the three components is 12 : 38 : 50 in weight.
packaging: 5 kg kits (A + B + C): component A: 0.6 kg; component B: 1.9 kg; component C: 2.5 kg.
storage: 12 months in its original, closed containers. Protect against frost and store at a temperature of at least 5°C.
notes: The two coating figures are per coat, and the sheet says to apply the product in two (criss-cross) coats, so the total for a normal application is twice the per-coat figure; the sheet does not print a total. The sheet does not say whether the per-coat figures refer to the mixed A+B+C product before or after the dilution water is added (water added after mixing: by brush 5-10%, by roller 10-15%, by spraying maximum of 20%). For the smoothing figure (1.5 kg/m² per mm) the sheet does not say whether it is Triblock P alone or the mortar of Triblock P plus quartz sand (the smoothing mortar is Triblock P with a maximum of 5% water and 0.25 Quartz or 0.5 Quartz at a ratio of 1 : 0.5 in weight); the printed density of the neat mix is 1,800 kg/m³, which would be 1.8 kg/m² per mm, so 1.5 is not simply the neat-mix density. Kit contents (0.6 + 1.9 + 2.5 = 5 kg) agree with the 12 : 38 : 50 ratio. The sixth whereToUse item is printed with a typo ('0.25 Quartz o 0.5 Quartz', 'o' for 'or') and is copied as printed. The first notFor item is a bulleted list in the sheet and is copied with the sheet's bullet characters. No standard or classification is stated. Floors or smoothing compound must be applied within 7 days of the primer.
